name: head injury overview
title: A head injury is a trauma patient first: the primary survey and the Glasgow Coma Scale grade it; a severe injury is acted on for herniation and sent for a STAT CT, which tells epidural, acute subdural, contusion, intracerebral hemorrhage and diffuse axonal injury or traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage apart, each with its own surgical rule; a concussion is a clinical diagnosis managed by removal, rest and a graded return

root.title: Head injury: a TRAUMA patient first
lines: A airway + C-spine precautions · B breathing · C circulation: large-bore IV, bloods for coagulopathy · D disability: neurological exam + Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) · E expose other injuries
GCS grades it: SEVERE 3-8 · MODERATE 9-12 · MILD 13-14 · MINOR 15
severe death by admission GCS: over 8 → 12% · 5-7 → 27% · under 5 → 78% · coma over 1 day 30-50% · intracranial pressure over 20 (normal under 15) → 50%
20 per 100,000 a year · peak 15-24 · young → car crashes · old → falls

groups.title: SEVERE traumatic brain injury
lines: edema, vasodilation, vascular congestion, hematoma → ↑ intracranial pressure → HERNIATION

pres.title: Herniating? Act, then a STAT CT
lines: • UNCAL: same-side fixed dilated pupil (third nerve) + opposite-side weakness
• TONSILLAR: medulla compressed → Cushing's triad (hypertension, bradycardia, apnea) · fatal
• intubate · head of the bed up · IV mannitol or 3% saline

head: h
Epidural hematoma
skull ↔ dura
middle meningeal ARTERY 50% · vein 33% · diploic vein, sinus 17%
clue: • NOT head acceleration · 33% another brain lesion
case: 19 y ejected · lucid in the ambulance · 2 h later right pupil fixed 7 mm, left hemiplegia · BP 160/90, pulse 55, apneic → craniotomy, recovered

head: h
Acute subdural hematoma
dura ↔ arachnoid
torn BRIDGING VEINS
clue: • a fall, head strikes a broad surface
• 10-15% of severe injuries · within 3 days · 30% of fatal ones
case: 75 y slipped on ice · comatose · right pupil fixed · decerebrate
tx: Death from the BRAIN injury beneath

head: h
Cerebral contusion
COUP under the impact: skull bends in, springs back
CONTRECOUP opposite it: acceleration
clue: • e.g. confusion, personality change, loss of smell
case: 43 y fell off a bike · confused, personality change, no smell · died of DVT at day 10
inv: usually several · repeat CT at 24-48 h: 20% bleed later

head: h
Intracerebral hemorrhage
deceleration or contact · 1-3%
frontal, temporal lobes 80-90%
clue: A confluent bleed in the brain
• blood dissects the brain around it
• the brain around it is normal

head: h
Diffuse axonal injury · traumatic SAH
ACCELERATION injury
often co-exist
clue: LOC at the scene → PERSISTENT coma
• axonal injury is 50% of severe brain injury
case: 43 y high-speed crash · GCS 4 at scene · persistent coma

head: h
Concussion
rotational acceleration · NO impact needed
81-92% no LOC · helmets don't prevent it
a chest blow can whiplash the brain
clue: • 85% of first ones recover in 1-4 weeks
• risk: young brain, FEMALE, a previous concussion
case: 17 y, soccer ball to the occiput · headache, neck pain · no LOC, GCS 15, no focal signs
inv: no CT, MRI, blood test or EEG · SCAT5: 1 of 22 symptoms
tx: when in doubt, remove from play, work, school
1 · mental + physical rest 24-48 h, not longer
2 · return to LEARN once symptom-free: part time, easiest classes, no phys ed
3 · return to PLAY after full-time school + medical clearance

panels.title: Herniation
items: UNCAL: same-side third nerve palsy, dilated pupil + opposite weakness
TONSILLAR: medulla compressed → fatal cardiorespiratory failure
descending: nerves III, IV, VI · PCA, ACA stroke · Duret hemorrhage

panels.title: Skull fractures
items: linear · depressed · open or closed: CONTACT injury
BASILAR: raccoon eyes · Battle sign · CSF from ear or nose · hemotympanum
basilar: may be missed on CT · risk of MENINGITIS

panels.title: Concussion: what can follow
items: post-concussion syndrome: over 2 weeks adults, 4 weeks youth → permanent removal
CTE: repeated concussions · tau tangles · NEUROPATHOLOGICAL diagnosis
prevent: no checks to the head, no headers · return-to-play protocol
